issues.explanation: This is an ordinary verb-complement phrase in context, not a lexicalized idiom; grouping it hides the useful complement 尽.
issues.suggested_fix: Split into 淘 and 尽.

issues.explanation: Here 桓 abbreviates 桓帝 in the paired historical reference 桓、灵帝, not the surname Huan.
issues.suggested_fix: Gloss as “Emperor Huan (abbreviated from 桓帝)”.

issues.explanation: In 宦官专权 this is a verb phrase meaning to monopolize or wield political power, not the noun “autocracy.”
issues.suggested_fix: Gloss as “to monopolize power” or “to wield exclusive power.”

issues.explanation: In 青蛇, 青 means green or blue-green; the Qinghai abbreviation is unrelated and misleading.
The local meaning is simply “snake”; the current gloss is not a learner-facing definition.
This is the place name Luoyang, but the current dictionary cross-reference does not explain it to the learner.
This is the place name Julu, and the current dictionary cross-reference is not a useful local gloss.
In 进山采药, 山 means “mountain”; it is not the surname Shan.
In 采药, 药 means medicine or medicinal herbs; “leaf of the iris” is unrelated here.
Here 南华 is part of the name or epithet 南华老仙, not the geographic meaning “South China.”
In 岁在甲子, 岁 means “year”; the current variant-entry gloss does not explain the word.
In 张梁称地公将军、人公将军, 称 means “to call” or “to name,” not “to fit.”
In 分路讨伐, 路 means route or direction; it is not the surname Lu.
